subject: Using uiOutput to show a long loading state. Is it possible?

messages.author: 2f94624d7ac6c2a0
messages.subject: Using uiOutput to show a long loading state. Is it possible?
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to use a uiOutput to give feedback to the user about the loading state of large R object. To do that, I try to change the uiOutput just before a long loading function is called, and I would like to change it again after the function exits.
I tried with something like this in my server.R

rv <- reactiveValues()

loadedResult <- reactive({
  if( input$loadButton > 0) {
 
    observe( rv$loadIndictaor <- "loading")

    temp <- loadFunction(object)

    observe( rv$loadIndicator <- NULL )

    return(temp)
  }
})

output$loadIndicatorUI <- renderUI ({
  if (is.null(rv$loadIndicator) ) {
    return NULL   
  }
  div(class="alert alert-info", rv$loadIndicator)
})


But the problem is that the loadIndicatorUI is not rendered before the loadFunction runs. The message 'loading' is only rendered after the loadFunction exits, thus making it meaningless.
Is there a way to get around this? I tried giving a high priority to the observer, but it did not change the behaviour.

Thanks all for your help!

Frederic

messages.subject: Re: Using uiOutput to show a long loading state. Is it possible?
parts:
The shinyIncubator package has a progress indicator that is designed for this purpose. Install it from GitHub like so:

if (!require("devtools"))
  install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("shiny-incubator", "rstudio")

In your ui.R, add library(shinyIncubator) at the top and progressInit() somewhere else in your UI (i.e. in mainPanel). It doesn't matter where you place progressInit, the progress widget is always pinned to the upper right of the screen.

For server.R, see ?withProgress for details.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Using uiOutput to show a long loading state. Is it possible?
parts: There are several problems here. If you don't use loadedResult anywhere, it won't execute; reactive expressions are lazily evaluated. And your usage of observe here is unnecessary; observe is used to execute and automatically re-execute a chunk of code whenever its reactive dependencies change. In this case, you're only assigning, so there are actually no reactive dependencies at all, so the observer code will just execute once and no more:

loadedResult <- reactive({
  if( input$loadButton > 0) {
 
    observe( rv$loadIndictaor <- "loading") 

    temp <- loadFunction(object)

    observe( rv$loadIndicator <- NULL )

    return(temp)
  }
})

This would be closer (but still won't work for reasons I describe below) (I put the NULL assignment inside on.exit so it is called even if an error occurs in loadFunction):

observe({
  if( input$loadButton > 0) {
    rv$loadIndictaor <- "loading"
    on.exit(rv$loadIndicator <- NULL)
    temp <- loadFunction(object)
    return(temp)
  }
})

The reason this doesn't help is because Shiny waits until all outputs are done computing and then pushes all the new values to the browser at once. We found that this was more intuitive behavior than updating the outputs one at a time. You can, however, send messages to the client without waiting for all the output to be ready, if you know JavaScript; see https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-incubator/blob/master/R/progress.R#L127 and https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-incubator/blob/master/inst/progress/progress.js#L35 for an example.
